title: Argentina’s Economic Chainsaw Massacre
gist: Jeremy Adelman argues Argentine President Javier Milei, a lynchpin of Trump's Latin America strategy, achieved recovery and relative price stability by driving millions into destitution, which could make him a weak link ahead of next year's elections. Excerpt only.

insights.claim: Javier Milei may be a lynchpin of Donald Trump's geoeconomic vision for Latin America but could soon become its weak link, because his economic recovery and relative price stability came by driving millions of Argentines into destitution.
insights.speaker: JEREMY ADELMAN
insights.so_what: Argentine political risk ahead of next year's elections could challenge a US-backed Latin America strategy.

insights.claim: Last year Trump extended Argentina an unprecedented $20 billion currency swap line to halt the peso's free fall on the eve of legislative elections, and Milei's party won a surprising victory.
insights.speaker: JEREMY ADELMAN
insights.so_what: US official support has been a key stabilizer for Argentine assets and could be politically contingent.

insights.claim: Brazil's right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro is promising an economic policy that would follow Milei's lead, and Trump calls Milei his 'favorite president'.
insights.speaker: JEREMY ADELMAN
insights.so_what: Milei's fortunes spill over into Brazilian election positioning and the regional right.
